description: Add graceful shutdown to cmd/main.go and propagate cancellation to the notification scheduler. Replace http.ListenAndServe with an *http.Server started in a goroutine, wait on a signal-driven context, and Shutdown with a 10s timeout. Independent of other features; touches only cmd/main.go.
steps: In cmd/main.go add imports: os/signal and syscall (context and time are already imported).

Near the start of main (before or just after config load), create the root context: `ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)` and `defer stop()`. (os is not yet imported — add it.)
Change the scheduler start from `scheduler.Start(context.Background())` to `scheduler.Start(ctx)` so the scheduler goroutine stops on signal.

Replace the final `if err := http.ListenAndServe(addr, router); err != nil { log.Fatalf(...) }` block with: construct `srv := &http.Server{Addr: addr, Handler: router}`; launch `go func() { if err := srv.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed { log.Fatalf("[MAIN] FATAL: Server error: %v", err) } }()`; log that the server is listening; then `<-ctx.Done()` to block until a signal; then build `shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)`, `defer cancel()`, and call `srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)`, logging success or the error.
Keep the chi router's /health route intact (it is served by `router`). The pre-existing http.HandleFunc("/health", ...) on DefaultServeMux may stay as-is.
acceptance_criteria: cmd/main.go no longer calls http.ListenAndServe directly; it uses an *http.Server with ListenAndServe in a goroutine and srv.Shutdown with a 10s timeout.
The notification scheduler receives the signal-driven ctx (not context.Background()).
The Docker gate command passes: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...
verification: docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app golang:1.22-bullseye sh -c "go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./..." — all pass. go vet must report no issues on the rewritten main.
findings: Implemented in cmd/main.go only. Added imports os, os/signal, syscall. Created root ctx via signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM) with defer stop() right after the pre-existing /health DefaultServeMux handler. scheduler.Start now receives ctx instead of context.Background(). Replaced http.ListenAndServe with srv := &http.Server{Addr: addr, Handler: router}; ListenAndServe runs in a goroutine (ignoring http.ErrServerClosed); logs listening; blocks on <-ctx.Done(); then srv.Shutdown with a 10s context.WithTimeout, logging success/error. The chi router /health route is untouched (served via router); the DefaultServeMux /health handler left as-is. Docker gate passed: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... all green (config, controllers, helpers tests ok; vet reported no issues). No user-visible behavior change beyond graceful shutdown.
